scope.notes: Inventory in progress (242 rows). Covers Exalted: The Sidereals character-creation overview (Chapter Three), the five Auspicious-Ability groups tied to the celestial constellations and their Celestial Hierarchy minimums, the universal caste-agnostic Anima Effect, all five Castes (Journeys, Serenity, Battles, Secrets, Endings) with their Anima Banners/Anima Effects/Caste Abilities/Associations/Sobriquets/Concepts, the Arcane Fate signature trait mechanic and its Sidereal Anima Banner visibility/Paradox table, the Craft (Fate) Ability specialty, the new/altered Backgrounds (Allies, Artifact, Backing, Familiar, Manse altered; Acquaintances, Celestial Manse, Connections, Salary, Savant, Sifu new), Chapter Five's general Charm framework (Manipulating Fate, Creatures Outside of Fate, Restricted Charms, Unusual Charms, Matters of Personality, Prayer Strips, Spotting Active Prayer Strips, On Memory, Presentation Format), all five Castes' full sets of Ability-line Charm trees (completing all 25 of Chapter Five's Caste-and-Ability Charm trees: Journeys 29 Charms, Serenity 30 Charms, Battles 31 Charms, Secrets 32 Charms, Endings 30 Charms including the Violet Bier of Sorrows Style), the general 'Sidereal Martial Arts' secret-style framework (including the Sutras resonance mechanic), and all three of the book's named secret Sidereal Martial Arts styles in full: Charcoal March of Spiders (12 Charms), Prismatic Arrangement of Creation (16 Charms), and Citrine Poxes of Contagion (13 Charms plus its tree-overview and Infectious Martial Arts/Spiritual Diseases framework rows), pp. 184-201/PDF 187-204. Also now covers the Sidereal Astrology (Colleges/constellations) system's rules framework (overview, Petitions paperwork, the Effect Roll procedure, Blessing/Curse effect types, Scope/Duration/Power tables, Multiple/Canceling Effects, Censure, Paradox, Pattern Bite, and the opening of the Procedure-and-Catalog-of-Colleges section), plus Resplendent Destinies (pp. 204-218/PDF 207-221). Remaining: the specific Colleges/constellations catalog itself (the named list of individual Colleges within the astrology system) and a check for Sidereal-specific Merits/Flaws.

sources.role: Primary Sidereal rules, Charms, Backgrounds, and setting material

rulesNotes: Printed page numbers in this book run 3 less than the PDF page number supplied (PDF page = printed page + 3) for the copy used to build this inventory. Confirmed consistently across Chapter Three: Character Creation (PDF pp. 99-103, printed pp. 96-100) and Chapter Four: Traits (PDF pp. 107-127, printed pp. 104-124); both page numbers are recorded on every citation.
This PDF is image-based (no selectable text layer); all rows below were transcribed from rendered page images, per the 'OCR is an extraction aid, never verification by itself' rule.

Sidereals do not have a Limit Trait. Unlike Abyssal Resonance, their signature trait mechanic (Arcane Fate) is not a numeric, rated Trait with discrete gain/loss procedures -- it is a passive, always-on effect every Sidereal has from Exaltation onward. It is inventoried as a single mechanic row plus its associated Sidereal Anima Banner visibility/Paradox table, rather than as gain/loss/manifestation rows the way Resonance was for Abyssal.

The Sidereal Curse (the Great Curse's Sidereal-specific expression) is confirmed to be a roleplaying-only element with no discrete mechanical trigger or penalty table of its own (Chapter Three, PDF p. 103/printed p. 100 sidebar: 'The Sidereal Curse has no mechanical aspect and is, instead, a matter entirely for roleplaying. See page 253 of the Storytelling chapter for more information.'). It is therefore out of scope for this core-mechanics pass; no row was created for it.

Resplendent Destinies (referenced repeatedly from the Arcane Fate section as the means by which a Sidereal can bypass her own Arcane Fate and don a memorable identity) are detailed in full on pp. 215-218 of this book, which have not been rendered or reviewed in this pass. Only the cross-cutting interaction described within the in-scope Arcane Fate section itself (PDF pp. 124-125) is captured here; the full Resplendent Destiny system is out of scope for this inventory.

docs/references/exalted1e/dragon-blooded/source-manifest.json already cites this same book once for a single externally-sourced Dragon-Blooded spell (Open the Spirit Door, Terrestrial Circle Sorcery, PDF p. 125-126/printed p. 122-123), flagged 'external-source' because this Sidereals PDF had not been supplied at the time. That citation was not modified or duplicated here; it remains Dragon-Blooded catalog content.

Confirmed the printed-page-equals-PDF-minus-3 offset continues to hold in Chapter Five (Charms and Martial Arts, starting printed p. 128/PDF 131), by cross-checking the printed folio numbers embedded in the rendered page images against the PDF page numbers used to render them.

Chapter Five's Charm material is organized very differently from the other four splats reviewed so far: rather than grouping Charms by Attribute or a small number of thematic trees, it presents one Charm tree per Caste-and-Auspicious-Ability combination (5 Castes x 5 Auspicious Abilities = 25 trees total), each opened by a short poetic 'Scripture of the (Maiden)' epigraph and a named tree title (e.g. 'Endurance -- The Mast' for Journeys Caste). This inventory has so far completed one full tree (Journeys: Endurance) as a template for the remaining 24; each will need the same page-by-page treatment.

A few rows in this round have mechanics text that reads ambiguously in the source and were paraphrased as faithfully as possible rather than smoothed over: the exact numeric difficulty-by-range table for Spotting Active Prayer Strips was not transcribed row-by-row, and the healing-rate wording in One Direction Invocation's description is confusingly phrased in the book itself. Both are flagged in their own row's notes for a closer re-read before promotion.

The Journeys Caste's remaining four Charm trees (Ride 'The Messenger', Sail 'The Captain', Survival 'The Ship's Wheel', Thrown 'The Gull') are now complete, closing out the full Journeys Caste at pp. 134-142/PDF 137-145. Several Charm descriptions span a tree-diagram page break in the source (stat block on one page, prose on the next); these were transcribed as single continuous Charms with a note on the page split. Adopting the Untamed Face's row cross-references Exalted: The Lunars' ikth-ya/murr-ya Lunar social-caste terminology, which is out of scope for this inventory and not independently verified here.

The Serenity Caste (Craft 'The Peacock', Dodge 'The Ewer', Linguistics 'The Pillar', Performance 'The Musician', Socialize 'The Lovers', pp. 143-153/PDF 146-156) and the Battles Caste (Archery 'The Quiver', Brawl 'The Gauntlet', Melee 'The Spear', Presence 'The Banner', Resistance 'The Shield', pp. 153-162/PDF 156-165) are now both complete, closing out two full Castes.

The Secrets Caste (Investigation 'The Key', Larceny 'The Guardians', Lore 'The Treasure Trove', Occult 'The Sorcerer' in two parts, Stealth 'The Mask', pp. 163-173/PDF 166-176) is now complete, closing out a third full Caste beyond Journeys and matching the same per-Ability tree format. Occult is unusual in presenting two separate tree diagrams under one Ability ('The Sorcerer I', a Charm-based branch, and 'The Sorcerer II', which grants access to Terrestrial/Celestial Circle sorcery); both are treated as one combined Ability-line tree for this count. Auspicious Prospects for (Caste) (Investigation tree) is a single Charm presented as five near-identical Maiden-specific variants; the source text explicitly names variants for Journeys, Serenity, Battles, and Fate (Secrets) but does not explicitly name an Endings variant, which is flagged in that row's notes rather than guessed. Terrestrial Circle Sorcery's stat block prints an apparently inconsistent 'Duration: Simple' value, transcribed as printed and flagged in that row's notes.

Only the Endings Caste's five Ability-line Charm trees remain uninventoried to complete all 25 of Chapter Five's Charm trees. The Endings Caste header ('Endings: The Violet Bier of Sorrows') and its first tree (Athletics, 'The Rising Smoke') begin at printed p. 174/PDF 177, immediately after Secrets Caste's Stealth tree ends; its second tree (Awareness, 'The Crow') begins at printed p. 175/PDF 178. Resume point for the next round: printed p. 175/PDF 178, partway through the Awareness tree (Prior Warning and Expected Pain charms already identified but not yet checked in).

The Endings Caste's five Ability-line Charm trees (Athletics 'The Rising Smoke', Awareness 'The Crow', Bureaucracy 'The Haywain', Martial Arts 'The Sword' (the Violet Bier of Sorrows Style, also called the Endings Form), and Medicine 'The Corpse', pp. 174-184/PDF 177-187) are now complete, closing out the fifth and final Caste and all 25 of Chapter Five's Caste-and-Ability Charm trees. The Martial Arts tree is this book's first Ability-line tree built around a dedicated Martial Arts style rather than a mundane Ability; a sidebar on printed p. 179/PDF 182 ('Staff and Blade') specifies that its Charms treat knife, sword, staff, seven-section-staff, and serpent-sting-staff attacks as unarmed attacks and that none of its Charms function while wearing armor, folded into the root Charm's (Secrets of Future Strife) notes rather than given its own row. Immediately after this tree, the book opens a general 'Sidereal Martial Arts' section (printed p. 184/PDF 187) describing further secret styles available to Sidereals specifically (Charcoal March of Spiders, Prismatic Arrangement of Creation, Citrine Pox of Contagion) — these are a distinct system from the 25 Caste-and-Ability trees and remain unrendered/uninventoried; Charcoal March of Spiders' tree diagram and framework text (but not yet its Charm-by-Charm mechanics) have been rendered as of this pass. Resume point for the next round: printed p. 185/PDF 188, at the start of Charcoal March of Spiders Style's Charm descriptions (Unnatural Many-Step Stride).

A ninth pass added the general 'Sidereal Martial Arts' framework (sidereal-martial-arts, covering the three secret styles' shared framing) and its Sutras resonance mechanic (sidereal-martial-arts-sutras), then completed the entire Charcoal March of Spiders Style (12 Charms plus its tree-overview row, pp. 185-190/PDF 188-193): three roots (Unnatural Many-Step Stride, Maw of Dripping Venom, Rain of Unseen Threads) feeding Dance of the Hungry Spider, Charcoal March of Spiders Form, and Nest of Living Strands, converging through Cannibalistic Heritage Technique on Jumping Spider Strike, which spreads to Thumbnail Spider March and Water Spider Bite and the capstone Grandmother Spider Mastery via Pattern Spider Touch. The pass then began Prismatic Arrangement of Creation Style (a 16-Charm tree built around the Five Magical Materials, pp. 190-191/PDF 193-194), completing its tree-overview row, its four root Charms (Deadly Starmetal Offensive, Orichalcum Sheathing Stance, Flickering Moonsilver Approach, Five Jade Fury) and its first Form Charm (Four Magical Materials Form, converging all four roots). Resume point for the next round: printed p. 191/PDF 194, continuing Prismatic Arrangement of Creation Style past Four Magical Materials Form (11 Charms remain in that tree), then Citrine Pox of Contagion Style (not yet located/rendered).

A tenth pass finished the rest of Prismatic Arrangement of Creation Style's 16-Charm tree (pp. 191-194/PDF 194-197): Four Magical Materials Form's two branches -- Charm Redirection Technique feeding Sequential Charm Disruption and Spell-Shattering Palm, and Astrology Interruption Method feeding Soul Fire Shaper Form -- converge (with Demesne Emulation Practice's Demesne and Manse Form) via God Ways/(Type) Exalt Ways and Games of Divinity Form on the capstone Prismatic Arrangement of Creation Form. It then located and fully inventoried the book's third and final named secret Sidereal Martial Arts style, Citrine Poxes of Contagion (pp. 195-201/PDF 198-204; note the book consistently spells it plural, 'Poxes,' not the singular 'Pox'): its tree-overview row and a separate Infectious Martial Arts/Spiritual Diseases framework row (covering the Mundane/Magical Treatment Difficulty system and the three Circles of spiritual illness severity), then all 13 Charms across two linked tree diagrams -- first diagram: Feverish Essence Discharge Atemi, Disjointed Essence Infectious Atemi, and Convulsive Displacement Infectious Atemi (three infectious-atemi roots) converging on Essence-Disrupting Infectious Atemi, alongside Perfect Reconstruction Method and Spirit and Body Purification Touch (two curative roots) converging on Flare of Invulnerability Method, with Spirit and Body Purification Touch also feeding Inner Dragon Unbinding, all three branches converging on the Form Charm Citrine Poxes of Contagion Form; second diagram: that Form feeds Spiritual Perfection, which feeds both Gentle Touch of the Wicked Hand and Glorious Sidereal Protection, converging on the capstone Essence-Shattering Typhoon. This closes out all three of the book's named secret Sidereal Martial Arts styles (Charcoal March of Spiders, Prismatic Arrangement of Creation, Citrine Poxes of Contagion). Resume point for the next round: printed p. 202/PDF 205 is a full-page illustration with no Charm content; the full Colleges/astrology system, Resplendent Destinies (pp. 215-218), and a check for Sidereal-specific Merits/Flaws all remain unrendered/uninventoried and their exact page locations within the remainder of the book (printed pp. 202-253+) have not yet been confirmed by rendering.

An eleventh pass located and inventoried the Sidereal Astrology (Colleges/constellations) rules system, printed pp. 204-218/PDF 207-221: the section overview (sidereal-astrology-overview), Petitions (the paperwork/calligraphy/co-and-countersignature procedure for casting an astrology effect), the Effect Roll (Determining, Formulating, and Activating Effects), the Blessing/Curse Effect Types split, the Effect Scope/Duration/Power tables, rules for Multiple Effects and Canceling Effects, Censure (the penalty for illicit/unauthorized astrology use), Paradox (astrology's equivalent to sorcerous backlash), and Pattern Bite (a lingering-consequence mechanic). Resplendent Destinies (resplendent-destinies, printed p. 215/PDF 218) was also inventoried as a single calculated row covering the full system (not just the earlier cross-reference from the Arcane Fate section). The pass then opened the 'Procedure for Sidereal Astrology and Catalog of Colleges' section (sidereal-astrology-procedure-and-catalog-overview, printed p. 218/PDF 221), which is the book's lead-in to the actual named-College catalog. Resume point for the next round: printed p. 218/PDF 221 (or the page immediately following, if that page is entirely the section's introductory text), continuing into the specific Colleges/constellations catalog itself -- the individual named Colleges (their Charm-tree-equivalent astrology-effect lists) have not yet been transcribed. A check for Sidereal-specific Merits/Flaws also remains outstanding.
